content.executive_summary:
- **Identity Verified**: Stefano Coda is Maître d'enseignement et de recherche (MER) at EPFL, Senior Scientist and head of the TCV tokamak group at the Swiss Plasma Center (SPC). Email stefano.coda@epfl.ch, office PPB 225, phone +41 21 693 3463. ORCID 0000-0002-8010-4971. LinkedIn: https://ch.linkedin.com/in/stefano-coda-a9781326. -> No namesake collision found; the physics publication record on TCV, ECRH/ECCD, fluctuation diagnostics, and JT-60SA is consistent and unique.
- **Recent Funding Signal**: A September 2024 EPFL news item describes a "two-year grant beginning in September 2024" tied to TCV experiments in negative-triangularity plasma scenarios; the funder is implied to be the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) via the EPFL/SPC press cycle, but the exact SNSF award ID, amount, currency, and role (PI vs. co-PI) were not directly verified in an SNSF award-database record. -> Treat as a strong but partial match until the SNSF project page is retrieved.
- **EUROfusion Framework Funding**: Multiple TCV papers and presentations by S. Coda (2023–2026) acknowledge EUROfusion Grant Agreement No. 101052200. This is a framework/multi-beneficiary consortium grant (not a single-PI competitive award) funding TCV operations within the European fusion roadmap. -> Listed as mission/consortium funding, not a personal competitive grant.
- **Open Positions (Active Hiring)**: A LinkedIn post dated 2025-03-19 from EPFL advertises "Diagnostic development and studies of turbulence and transport in the JT-60SA tokamak in Japan" hosted by Stefano Coda at EPFL (Lausanne, Vaud, Switzerland). -> Cross-checked against the SPC "Available positions" page; the page accepts rolling PhD applications and lists open topics.
- **Closed/Historical Posting**: No verified closed/historical postings published on or after 2026-01-01 were located for Coda or the TCV group in the public sources checked.
- **Confidence Caveat**: Direct SNSF/SNSF-data portal and EUROfusion project-database hits naming Coda as PI with a precise amount/award ID were not retrieved in the available search budget; the strongest primary evidence is the EPFL press item and the EUROfusion acknowledgement line in his papers. -> Where amounts or roles could not be confirmed, this is stated explicitly.
